score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current official utility/regulator guidance, explicit separation of strategic network planning from site-specific capacity/connection evidence and current-date controls.

sources.label: Thames Water water and wastewater capacity
sources.fact: Developers are advised to make a pre-planning enquiry; Thames Water states it can confirm network capacity within three weeks and discuss actions/timelines if capacity is unavailable. Generic service-area presence is not a capacity confirmation.

sources.label: Water resources planning guideline
sources.fact: Updated 16 June 2026; provides statutory planning framework for secure sustainable water supply and demand forecasting, but is not a site connection assessment.

sources.label: Drainage and Wastewater Management Plan guidance
sources.fact: Sewerage undertakers have a statutory duty to prepare, publish and maintain DWMPs; strategic plans do not substitute for development-specific wastewater capacity evidence.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy SI2
sources.fact: Major development follows the energy hierarchy and should include a detailed energy strategy; policy compliance is distinct from an electricity connection offer.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy SI3 Energy infrastructure
sources.fact: Large-scale development should engage early with energy bodies and identify electricity/gas infrastructure requirements; strategic planning is not evidence of available connection capacity.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy SI5 Water infrastructure
sources.fact: Development proposals should ensure adequate wastewater capacity; growth locations with insufficient capacity should use integrated water management strategies and work with Thames Water.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy SI6 Digital connectivity
sources.fact: New development should provide full-fibre-capable infrastructure or equivalent and meet mobile-connectivity demand; policy requirement is not current network-service confirmation.

sources.label: Ofgem demand connections reform update
sources.fact: Published 16 June 2026; Ofgem states the demand queue is large and includes projects unable to connect quickly due to network/generation build and non-viable blockers.

sources.label: Ofgem strategic energy planning and connections reform 2026
sources.fact: Published 21 April 2026; strategic planning and connection reform are evolving through 2026, so national reform status cannot be treated as a site connection date.

sources.label: Ofgem direction on NESO network planning
sources.fact: Published 17 July 2026; first CSNP is required by 15 December 2028 and will provide coordinated long-term whole-system planning.

sources.label: Ofgem ED3 investment rules
sources.fact: Published 21 May 2026; ED3 rules govern assessment of DNO 2028-33 investment plans, not present parcel-level capacity.

sources.label: Ofgem NESO role
sources.fact: NESO plans and coordinates electricity networks at system level; its strategic role does not replace a DNO/site-specific connection assessment.

examples.result: Thames Water service-area presence is not capacity evidence; a development-specific pre-planning enquiry remains required.
WRMP and DWMP strategic planning evidence cannot be converted into water/wastewater headroom for a parcel.
London Plan SI5 requires adequate wastewater capacity and early integrated planning where constrained; no assumed capacity fill.
Ofgem demand-queue reform explicitly confirms connection delay/non-viability issues; queue reform is not a connection offer.
CSNP 2028 planning horizon is tagged future strategic planning and not used as current network availability.
ED3 2028-33 investment rules are future network-planning context, not current site headroom.
Digital-connectivity policy requirement does not prove full-fibre/mobile service at an exact parcel.
No utilities promotion occurs without exact site relation plus current capacity/connection evidence from the relevant network operator.
